struck: South Carolina's standard home contract, Form 310 (9/2023)
use: (name no version on the page; the ledger's source is Form 310 (03/2026), which replaced the 9/2023 form on March 9, 2026)

struck: The state contract says whether a home warranty is provided and who pays for it.
use: The standard contract has no home warranty clause. Buyer and seller can add one with a separate addendum.

struck: On the form's default, a special assessment the association approved before closing is the seller's.
use: For a special assessment approved before closing, the contract has two boxes: the seller pays all of it, or only the part due in the year of closing. One approved after closing is the buyer's.

struck: Its own footer says the association makes no claim the form fits a given sale.
use: The form tells both sides they are responsible for getting legal advice before they sign.

struck: Horry County home sellers paid about $18 million in deed stamps in a year.
use: By the state's formula, the deed stamps on the 13,194 home sales recorded in Horry County from October 2025 through September 2026 come to about $18 million.

unless: \bif (?:there is|you have|it has)\b|\bwith a mortgage\b|\bmortgage to (?:release|pay off)\b
struck: On the middle $350,000 home, the costs set by law and the state contract come to $1,320.
use: On the middle $350,000 home with a mortgage to release, the costs set by law and the state contract come to $1,320.

struck: Outside city limits, Horry County's 2026 levy is 201.0 mills.
use: For most homes outside city limits, Horry County's 2026 levy is 201.0 mills.

struck: So a long-time owner's bill, and the tax credit at closing, is usually smaller than one figured on the price.
use: So when a home's last deed is old, its tax bill, and the tax credit at closing, is often smaller than one figured on today's price.

struck: Once asked, the loan servicer must send an accurate payoff statement within seven business days.
use: On a home loan made for personal use, the servicer must send an accurate payoff statement within seven business days of a written request. A loan made to buy a rental is not covered by that rule.

struck: South Carolina bars a transfer fee recorded after February 2012 that sends money to a third party on each sale.
use: South Carolina bars a transfer fee covenant recorded after February 1, 2012 that makes an owner pay a third party on each sale.

struck: Of 3,689 houses for sale in our area at $50,000 or more, about 3 in 10 list no HOA fee; every condo has one. So most sellers here will have an association's charges on their closing statement.
use: Of about 3,060 houses for sale in Horry County ZIPs, about 830 (more than 1 in 4) list no HOA fee. All but one of 2,686 condos for sale list one.

struck: About 6 in 10 Horry County condo owners, and about 1 in 5 house owners, get their tax bill at an address outside South Carolina.
use: About 6 in 10 Horry County condo units, and about 1 in 5 other homes, have their tax bill mailed to an address outside South Carolina.

struck: Of 2,157 resale houses and townhouses for sale in Horry County, 1,304 (about 6 in 10) have already cut their asking price ... about 7 in 10 under $300,000 (339 of 492).
use: Of 2,187 resale houses and townhouses for sale in Horry County, 1,264 (nearly 6 in 10) have cut their asking price: about 2 in 3 under $300,000 (325 of 498), 403 of 707 from $300,000 to $450,000, 311 of 563 to $700,000 and 225 of 419 above. For resale condos it is about half (1,347 of 2,627).

struck: Home warranties are a builder's offer here, not a seller's habit. Of 1,028 houses and townhouses ... 965 are new construction. Only 63 of 2,157 resale houses (about 1 in 33) offer one.
use: Of 1,000 houses and townhouses for sale in Horry County that advertise a home warranty, 935 are new construction. Only 65 of 2,187 resale houses (about 3 in 100) advertise one, and 33 of 2,627 resale condos.
